title: Growing Together transit-area zoning framework adopted
subtitle: Also: inclusionary zoning, 490 Huron Road towers, Francis Street heritage designation withdrawn, Bramm Street parking deferred.
overview: Council finished a very long night by adopting the Growing Together land use and zoning framework for seven Protected Major Transit Station Areas, unanimously. Staff estimate it could allow more than 100,000 new homes at about half of full zoning capacity. Council raised the SGA3 height limit from 25 to 28 storeys {{vote:m6}}, kept the tower separation rules staff proposed, and asked for a housekeeping review after the Official Plan is complete.

Council also approved inclusionary zoning in the same areas, which requires some affordable units in new buildings. Two downtown properties were held back until a special meeting on March 25. Council approved a 24-storey Official Plan and zoning change at 490 Huron Road, despite residents' complaints about notice. It also dropped a proposed heritage designation for 70 Francis Street North after the owner objected.

Other items: a decision on Bramm Street parking rates was deferred to the next meeting, and Council will ask the province to extend the heritage-listing deadline to 2030. Council also approved the Hidden Valley Road development and three new heritage designation notices.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the official plan and zoning amendments for seven transit station areas, as amended, and directed staff to return with a housekeeping review once the Official Plan is complete.
Council raised the SGA3 maximum height from 25 to 28 storeys, except for properties subject to a declared conflict, which were voted on separately.

Council adopted inclusionary zoning in the transit station areas, with a memorandum of understanding with the Region and reviews in 2024, 2026, 2028 and 2030, and deferred two Park and Victoria Street properties to March 25.
Council adopted the Official Plan amendment allowing up to 24 storeys and approved the matching zoning by-law amendment.
Council sustained the owner's objection and withdrew the notice of intention to designate the property as heritage.
Council will call on the province to extend the Ontario Heritage Act deadline for removing listed properties from the register from January 2025 to January 2030.
Council deferred the delegation request on Bramm Street evening and weekend parking rates to the next meeting so Council can talk further with staff.
Council adopted the Official Plan amendment, approved the zoning change as amended and granted draft condominium plan approval.

debate: Bramm Street delegates said the lot is downtown and should be treated like other downtown surface lots with free evenings and weekends. They cited a lack of notice, confusing parking signage and the effect on nearby businesses and visitors. Staff said the free-parking subsidy was created for businesses hurt by LRT construction, and that the parking enterprise faces a deficit of about $1.5 million.

On Growing Together, staff defended 25 storeys and the tower separation rules as part of a balanced package and said they had not assessed 28 storeys. Supporters of the increase pointed to recent applications at 27 to 32 storeys and the need to ease the housing supply crisis. Others worried that higher limits could not easily be reversed.

Amendments to limit upzoning in heritage districts, protect affordable housing and rezone heritage-designated properties all failed. Staff said existing heritage tools still apply and that rezoning to lower densities had not been given public notice.

The owner of 70 Francis Street North said designation would raise repair, insurance and resale costs for a low-income rental building. Several councillors were sympathetic to the burden on owners. Staff said the property met four of the nine provincial criteria.

Residents said they did not hear about the 490 Huron Road changes in time and asked for an in-person public meeting. Staff said notices went well beyond the required distance, and a deferral could lead to an appeal. Several councillors said a deferral would not change the outcome.
